title: They thought holiness meant staying away from sinners.
paragraphs: They thought holiness meant staying away from sinners.
So when Jesus sat down to eat with them… it shocked everyone.

Tax collectors.
Outcasts.
People with reputations.
The kind of people religious leaders avoided.
And that table in Matthew 9 became a battlefield between two visions of religion.

One built on performance.
The other built on mercy.
The Pharisees saw it and immediately asked the question that still echoes in churches today:

“Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
(Matthew 9:11)
In their mind, holy people separate themselves.

Distance equals righteousness.
Association equals compromise.
But Jesus was about to expose a deeper problem.
Not in the sinners.
In the religious.
So He answered with a line that cut through centuries of empty religion:

“Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.’ For I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.”
— Matthew 9:12–13
Pause for a moment.
Jesus didn’t say sacrifice was useless.
The Old Testament sacrificial system was commanded by God Himself.
But something had gone terribly wrong.
The Pharisees had mastered ritual but lost compassion.

They could quote the Law…
But they could not love the broken.
They brought offerings to the temple.
Yet they had no mercy for the people those offerings were meant to point toward.
That’s why Jesus quoted Hosea 6:6, where God rebuked Israel:
“For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.”
The issue was never obedience.
The issue was a heart that performs religion without reflecting God’s character.
And God’s character is full of mercy.
This is the scandal of the Gospel.
Jesus didn’t build His ministry around the morally impressive.
He walked toward the spiritually sick.

The addict.
The ashamed.
The liar.
The tax collector who cheated people.
The woman with a past that everyone whispered about.
Those were the people sitting at His table.
Not because their sin didn’t matter.
But because they knew they needed a Savior.
And that’s the difference.
Self-righteous people think they are healthy.
Broken people know they need a physician.
Jesus said He came for the sick.
Not the self-congratulating.
Not the religious performers who believe their moral résumé earns them favor with God.
He came for sinners.
Which means the door of grace swings wide open for people who feel disqualified.
If you feel like your past is too messy…
If you feel like your failures are too public…
If you feel like you’ve disappointed God too many times…
Matthew 9 says something stunning:
You are exactly the kind of person Jesus came for.
But the story doesn’t stop at mercy.
Because mercy is not God pretending sin doesn’t exist.
Mercy is God dealing with sin through the cross of Christ.
The sacrifices of the Old Testament were shadows pointing to something greater.
Every lamb offered on the altar whispered the same message:
“Sin requires a price.”
And one day, Jesus Himself would become the final sacrifice.
The spotless Lamb.
The sinless Son of God.
At the cross, justice and mercy collided.
God did not ignore sin.
He paid for it.
Jesus took the punishment sinners deserved so that mercy could flow freely to anyone who repents and believes.
That’s the Gospel.
Not self-improvement.
Not religious performance.
Not spiritual reputation management.
Salvation by grace through faith in Christ alone.
And when that grace truly changes a heart, something beautiful happens.
Mercy begins to overflow.
The forgiven become forgiving.
The rescued become compassionate.
The people who once needed grace become the ones who extend it.
This is why Jesus told the Pharisees:
“Go and learn what this means.”
In other words:

You’ve studied Scripture.
Now learn the heart of God.
Because a religion that sacrifices animals but refuses to love people has missed the entire point.
And let’s be honest.
The same danger still exists today.

We can attend church…
Quote Bible verses…
Defend theology online…
Yet still carry hearts that are cold toward sinners.
But Jesus moves toward them.
He sits at the table.
He calls Matthew the tax collector.
He restores Peter after failure.
He forgives the woman caught in adultery.
And He still calls people today.
Not the perfect.
The repentant.
So here’s the question that Matthew 9 forces every one of us to answer:
Are we building a religion of sacrifice without mercy?
Or are we following the Savior who rescues sinners?
Because the Gospel is not a club for the morally superior.
It is a hospital for the spiritually sick.
And Jesus is still the Great Physician.
Still healing.
Still forgiving.
Still calling people out of darkness and into life.
The invitation is the same today as it was at that table.
Come honestly.
Come humbly.
Come repentant.
And discover the mercy of Christ.
Because Jesus did not come to call the righteous.
He came to call sinners.
And that is the best news the world has ever heard.
God’s mercy is greater than our worst sin.
